clue.text: Make a slope for beetle, about a metre

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the beetle's name is wrapped round the metre

parts.note: a chafer is a kind of beetle, as in cockchafer

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a ramp for a beetle, roughly a metre long.
explanation.definitionFit: To chamfer is to bevel an edge, cutting it at an angle so that it slopes.

clue.text: Christian policeman has sound credit

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: sound means the word for credit is taken as it is pronounced, not as spelt

parts.note: buying on tick means buying on credit

explanation.surface: A churchgoing officer has a good credit rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit; TIC sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coptic Church is the ancient Christian church of Egypt.

clue.text: Is a name recollectable?.Not with this

definitions.text: Is a name recollectable?.Not with this

indicators.note: recollectable is read as able to be re-collected, so the letters of is a name are gathered again in a new order

explanation.surface: A question about remembering a name, answered: not if you have this condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the condition and the first three words, rearranged, spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, so a sufferer cannot recall names.

clue.text: Imitator, it's said, of a more downright king.

parts.note: downright means flat, as in a flat refusal, so more downright is flatter
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Someone who copies, people say, a blunter monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the proverb that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery, so an imitator is said to be a flatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who copies you pays you a compliment, according to the old saying.

clue.text: Method of dating broadcast on coal

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: radio is broadcasting by sound
coal is largely carbon

explanation.surface: A dating technique is announced on air about coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeologists date organic remains by measuring decay of carbon-14.

clue.text: Is it like a Russian to be unoriginal?

explanation.surface: A question about whether copying is a national trait of Russians.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as SLAV-ISH, the word means somewhat like a Slav, such as a Russian; as one word it means imitative.
explanation.definitionFit: Russians are Slavs, so something Slav-like is literally Slavish; slavish also means copying without independent thought.

clue.text: Her other case-book

explanation.surface: A reference to a woman's second casebook.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar the pronoun her (object case) has she as its other (subject) case; She is also a novel by H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: The nominative of the pronoun her is the subject form; Rider Haggard's adventure novel has that single-word title.

clue.text: Tree-god executed

indicators.note: executed is read as beheaded, so the god loses his first letter

parts.note: Balder is the Norse god of light

explanation.surface: A god of trees has been put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joins 'Tree' and 'god' in the surface, but 'Tree' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a deciduous tree of the birch family that grows near water.

clue.text: American doctor's home call sequence

parts.note: at home is in

indicators.note: call is read as calling out, so the word for sequence is taken as it sounds

parts.note: in turn means in sequence, one after another

explanation.surface: A US doctor's house phone has a list of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call' signals the sound: TERNE is said like TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US an interne (intern) is a junior hospital physician in training.

clue.text: Folksy poems translated into German

indicators.note: into means the rearranged poems go inside the word for German

parts.note: Hun is an old derogatory term for a German

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters of poems are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rustic verses rendered into German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' makes OMESP from POEMS, which goes 'into' HUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something homespun is simple and unsophisticated, like homemade cloth.

clue.text: With bowl, manage to beg

parts.note: a pan is a bowl-shaped vessel
to handle a situation is to manage it

explanation.surface: Someone uses a bowl to manage their begging.
explanation.definitionFit: To panhandle is American slang for begging in the street.

clue.text: Corporation lawyer is first to get information

indicators.note: the lawyer is placed first, ahead of the belly

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
corporation is old jocular slang for a large belly, so TUM

explanation.surface: A company lawyer is the first to receive the inside facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business but is old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of data, a fact given as information.

clue.text: Small picture of popular group

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be in
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A little photograph of a well-liked band.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small illustration placed within a larger one on a page or map.

clue.text: How to make Mars put down weapons?

parts.note: the letters of arms put in a different order spell the war god's name, so the command describes how to arrange them

explanation.surface: How does one persuade the god of war to disarm?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: put the letters of ARMS in order to make MARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Order arms is the drill command to bring a rifle down to rest upright beside the right foot.

clue.text: It condemned Luther's. teaching, but Robin lives by it

explanation.surface: A body that condemned Luther, also what a robin survives on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diet of Worms was the 1521 assembly in the German city of Worms that condemned Luther; a robin eats a diet of worms.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperial assembly of 1521 declared Luther an outlaw; garden birds such as robins feed on earthworms.

clue.text: Union recruitment office?

parts.note: union suggests a trade union signing up members, but here it is matrimony and the office finds partners

explanation.definitionFit: An agency that introduces people seeking a spouse recruits them for the union of wedlock.

clue.text: Diplomats no longer sharp — not how things should be

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a body of diplomats
in music a natural sign cancels a sharp

explanation.surface: Diplomats have lost their edge, which is not right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnatural departs from what is normal or proper.

clue.text: Mad about drilling installation for water

indicators.note: about means the angry word is wrapped round the rig

parts.note: mad in the sense of angry, so irate
an oil rig is a drilling installation

explanation.surface: Anger over an oil rig needing water.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply it with water by channels.

clue.text: Bruce making toast for poet

parts.note: Robert the Bruce was the medieval king of Scotland
making toast is browning bread under the grill

explanation.surface: Bruce prepares toast for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning was a Victorian poet; Robert the Bruce was the Scottish king who won at Bannockburn.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning wrote The Pied Piper of Hamelin and My Last Duchess among other verse.

clue.text: Engage a little woman to bury the rubbish

indicators.note: to bury means the woman's name surrounds the rubbish

parts.note: Beth is one of the March sisters in Little Women
rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Hire a petite woman to dispose of the junk.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel about the four March sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to promise in marriage, to make engaged.

clue.text: Cowardly Englishmen found out about this time

definitions.text: Cowardly Englishmen found out about this time

parts.words: Cowardly Englishmen found out about this time
parts.note: Noel Coward's song says mad dogs and Englishmen go out in the midday sun, so the Coward Englishmen are out at this hour

explanation.definitionFit: Midday is the hour at which, in Noel Coward's lyric, Englishmen go out in the sun.

clue.text: Tale of a foot?

explanation.surface: A question about a story concerning a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: A foot is the end of a leg, so LEG END; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story; the foot is where the leg finishes.

clue.text: Aware how Kent got into difficulties when batting first

indicators.note: first puts the batting piece at the front of the answer

parts.note: a cricket side that is batting is said to be in

indicators.note: getting into difficulties suggests things going awry, so the letters of how and Kent are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cricket report on how the Kent side struggled when they batted first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got into difficulties' makes THEKNOW from HOW and KENT. Kent is an English county with a first-class cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in possession of inside information is said to be well informed.

clue.text: Right for boy to hold hands

indicators.note: to hold means the boy's name wraps round the hands

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward
hands are workers, men

explanation.surface: It is proper for a boy to hold hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a text is to correct it, removing errors.

clue.text: Shanghai, say, is recurrent in metaphor

indicators.note: recurrent is read as running back, so the letters are taken from the end to the start

parts.note: Shanghai is an example of a port in the East, giving E (East) and PORT

explanation.surface: A Chinese city keeps cropping up in figurative language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrent' turns EPORT round. 'Shanghai' may suggest kidnapping sailors, but it is an eastern port.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, such as a metaphor, in which words are used in a non-literal way.

clue.text: Drink's around, working abandoned.

indicators.note: around means the drink is placed round the other piece

parts.note: ale is a drink; the 's is just a link
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone ordered a round of drinks and has walked off the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left by everyone else is solitary and deserted.

clue.text: Say foul words to hit back in game

indicators.note: back means the whole string of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG
dirt can mean obscene talk or smut
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: Swear in order to retaliate during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EGDIRTRAP round. 'game' means birds shot for sport, not a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a bird shot for sport, so it counts as game.

clue.text: Pulse starts to pound — energetic athlete

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: An athlete's heartbeat begins to pound with effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, of which the pea is one.

clue.text: Australian animal chained on the rocks

indicators.note: a ship on the rocks is wrecked, so the letters of chained are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An Australian creature is tied up on rocky ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is the spiny anteater, an egg-laying mammal native to Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Hurried about to arrange table. for spread

indicators.note: about means the hurried word goes round the other piece

parts.note: sped is the past tense of speed, so hurried
to lay the table is to set it out for a meal

explanation.surface: Someone rushed around setting the table for a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something splayed is spread out wide, like fingers or legs.
